Given two Hilbert spaces H¹ and H², consider the space H=H¹+H² = { g + h | g∈H¹, g∈H²} with the norm

∣∣f∣∣=inf⁡f=g+h∣∣g∣∣+∣∣h∣∣ ||f|| = \inf_{f=g+h} ||g|| + ||h||∣∣f∣∣=f=g+hinf​∣∣g∣∣+∣∣h∣∣

If H¹ and H² are disjoint, then I can use IsHilbertSum. However, I am interested in the non-disjoint case. My loogling didn't find an implementation of this, also not for general normed vector spaces. Is there code for this?

If you're talking about a nondisjoint situation then you should probably be more precise about what the question is. Are these Hilbert spaces both subspaces of a common vector space? A common Hilbert space? Are they closed? Do the two norms on the intersection coincide etc? The best way to ask your question is with a #mwe .

It's for the sum of two RKHS. Conditions in books on that don't really mention it, but it is the same construction as used at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation_space. So, the Hilbert spaces are continuously embedded into the same Hausdorff topological vector space.

RKHS with bounded kernel embed continuously into the continuous functions. So, as an example we can take H¹ and H² are RHKS over the same set X with bounded kernels, and then they are both subspace of the common vector space C_b(X).

If you are suppressing conditions because the books "don't really mention it" then you're going to have a hard job conveying what your precise question is, and Lean can only work with precise questions (unless you're lucky enough to run into an expert who can understand what you're saying because they already know the area). It would be better to ask your precise question with a #mwe or you run the risk of people putting effort into answering questions which turn out to be the wrong question. One thing I'm still not clear on is whether a function in both subspaces is guaranteed to have the same norm in both subspaces. From the Wikipedia page you link to it seems that the answer to this might be "no". I am a bit concerned about what happens if H^1 maps continuously into H^2 with e.g. dense image, so then the vector space sum would just be H^2 but now the norm might be completely messed up. But as I say I am still unclear as to exactly what you're asking.

The question that I have is whether the definition of interpolation couple / admissable pair and the associated theorem (above called proposition C.1.3) are part of mathlib.

What I want to use it for

The statement that I want to prove that relies on this is

Let XXX be a set, and UUU a Hilbert space. If K1,K2:X×X→L(U)K_1, K_2 : X\times X\to L(U)K1​,K2​:X×X→L(U) are positive semi-definite and H1,H2H_1,H_2H1​,H2​ the associated RKHS, then H≃H1⊕H2H\simeq H_1\oplus H_2H≃H1​⊕H2​ where HHH is the RKHS associated with the kernel K=K1+K2K=K_1+K_2K=K1​+K2​.
Here, ⊕\oplus⊕ is not the direct sum, but this non-disjointed direct sum.

In lean, RKHS and kernels are represented using

/--
A reproducing kernel Hilbert space is a Hilbert space with an
injection to functions mapping into another Hilbert space, such that point evaluation is continuous.
-/
class RKHS (𝕜 : outParam Type*) (H : Type*) (X V : outParam Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
    [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] where
  /-- Continuous injection to functions from the reproducing kernel Hilbert space `H` to functions
  from the domain `X` to the Hilbert space `V` -/
  coeCLM (𝕜) : H →L[𝕜] X → V
  coeCLM_injective : Function.Injective (coeCLM : H → X → V)

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {X : Type*}
variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V]
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H]
variable [RKHS 𝕜 H X V]

variable (H) in
def kerFun (x : X) : V →L[𝕜] H := (.proj x ∘L coeCLM 𝕜).adjoint
variable (H) in
def kernel : Matrix X X (V →L[𝕜] V) := .of fun x y ↦ (kerFun H x).adjoint ∘L kerFun H y

So, the statement would become something like

theorem ofKernel_sum_iso_sum_ofKernel { H₁ H₂ : Type* }
    [NormedAddCommGroup H₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H₁] [CompleteSpace H₁]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H₂] [CompleteSpace H₂]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] [CompleteSpace H]
    [RKHS 𝕜 H₁ X V] [RKHS 𝕜 H₂ X V] [RKHS 𝕜 H X V]
    (hK : kernel H = kernel H₁ + kernel H₂) :
    H ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] H₁ ⊕ H₂ := by
  sorry

If not present

If this sum is not present, I am happy to create a PR for it. I can image that the pair and the resulting space can be encoded using 

variable (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
variable (X₀ : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X₀] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X₀] [CompleteSpace X₀]
variable (X₁ : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X₁] [CompleteSpace X₁]

def InterpolationCouple
    : Prop :=
  ∃ (X : Type*) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : T2Space X) (_ : AddCommMonoid X) (_ : Module 𝕜 X),
  ∃ (emb₀ : X₀ →L[𝕜] X) (emb₁ : X₁ →L[𝕜] X),
    Function.Injective emb₀ ∧ Function.Injective emb₁

def Add (hC : InterpolationCouple 𝕜 X₀ X₁) : (X₀ × X₁) →L[𝕜] ??? := sorry

def CoupleSum (hC : InterpolationCouple 𝕜 X₀ X₁) := (X₀ × X₁) / (Add hC).ker

I have put question marks in Add because I don't know a good way to deal with the existence of the space X as part of the definition of an operator. Doing 

def CoupleSum (hC : InterpolationCouple 𝕜 X₀ X₁) : Type* :=
  let X     := Classical.choose hC
  let hX    := Classical.choose_spec hC
  let hTop  := Classical.choose_spec hX
  let := Classical.choose hX
  let hT2   := Classical.choose_spec hTop
  let := Classical.choose hTop
  let hGrp  := Classical.choose_spec hT2
  let := Classical.choose hT2
  let hMod  := Classical.choose_spec hGrp
  let emb₀  := Classical.choose hMod
  let hMod' := Classical.choose_spec hMod
  let emb₁  := Classical.choose hMod'
  {x : X // ∃ x₀ : X₀, ∃ x₁ : X₁, emb₀ x₀ + emb₁ x₁ = x}

at least doesn't seem to be the right thing.

I don't think opening a PR is a good idea. On one hand this notion is very specific, and on the other hand embedding a Banach space in something it Is not itself a Banach space looks like something that needs a careful design choice. If you need it in your project just go for it without thinking too much about mathlib!

I happen to have thought a year ago about what the statements of interpolation theory should look like. While this presentation is indeed quite typical, I prefer the following (non-standard) approach.

Say that a compatibility data on a pair X=(X0,X1)\mathbf{X} = (X_0, X_1)X=(X0​,X1​) of Banach spaces is the data of an auxiliary vector space ΔX\Delta_{\mathbf{X}}ΔX​ and injections of Δ\DeltaΔ in each XiX_iXi​ such that the antidiagonal {(x,−x)∣x∈ΔX}\{(x, -x) | x\in\Delta_{\mathbf{X}}\}{(x,−x)∣x∈ΔX​} is closed in X0×X1X_0 \times X_1X0​×X1​.

If X0X_0X0​ and X1X_1X1​ embed in some Hausdorff TVS then you can just take ΔX\Delta_{\mathbf{X}}ΔX​ to be the intersection of their images.

Once you have such a data, the associated "sum" is the quotient Banach space of the L1-sum X0⊕X1X_0 \oplus X_1X0​⊕X1​ by the antidiagonal subspace written above.

Going back to your actual question, I don't know much about RKHSs, but somehow it feels like what you want to do is push a norm through a surjective map. I think it will be a bit painful in the current state of the library, but I can try to finish #34106 if needed

@Anatole Dedecker, I gave it a go with an embedding space. What do you think about the construction? The names of things are just placeholders, i.e. we need to come up with better names for them.

universe u

variable (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
variable (F₀ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup F₀] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F₀]
variable (F₁ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F₁]

structure EmbeddingSpace' where
  carrier : Type
  [topologicalSpace  : TopologicalSpace carrier]
  [t2Space   : T2Space carrier]
  [addCommGroup  : AddCommGroup carrier]
  [continuousAdd : ContinuousAdd carrier]
  [mod : Module 𝕜 carrier]
  emb₀  : F₀ →L[𝕜] carrier
  emb₁  : F₁ →L[𝕜] carrier
  inj₀  : Function.Injective emb₀
  inj₁  : Function.Injective emb₁

instance : CoeSort (EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) Type :=
  ⟨EmbeddingSpace'.carrier⟩

instance (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : TopologicalSpace E.carrier   := E.topologicalSpace
instance (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : T2Space E.carrier            := E.t2Space
instance (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : AddCommGroup E.carrier       := E.addCommGroup
instance (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : Module 𝕜 E.carrier           := E.mod
instance (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : ContinuousAdd E.carrier      := E.continuousAdd


abbrev InterpolationCouple' : Prop := Nonempty (EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁)

abbrev ℓ1 := WithLp 1 (F₀ × F₁)

infixr:25 " ×₁ " => ℓ1

variable {F₀ F₁ 𝕜}

def coupleAdd (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) : (F₀ ×₁ F₁) →L[𝕜] E :=
    (E.emb₀.coprod E.emb₁).comp (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 1 𝕜 F₀ F₁).toContinuousLinearMap

abbrev CoupleSum (hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) := (coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).range

abbrev CoupleInter (hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) :=
    (Classical.choice hC).emb₀.range ⊓ (Classical.choice hC).emb₁.range

abbrev CoupleSum.Quotient (E : EmbeddingSpace' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) := (F₀ ×₁ F₁) ⧸ (coupleAdd E).ker

instance (hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) :
    IsClosed ((coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).ker : Set (F₀ ×₁ F₁))  :=
  (coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).isClosed_ker

noncomputable instance instNormedAddCommGroup (hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) :
    NormedAddCommGroup (CoupleSum hC) :=
  NormedAddCommGroup.induced
    (CoupleSum hC)
    (CoupleSum.Quotient (Classical.choice hC))
    (coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).quotKerEquivRange.symm.toAddMonoidHom
    (coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).quotKerEquivRange.symm.injective

lemma dist_zero_eq_norm {Q : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup Q] (a : Q) : dist 0 a = ‖a‖ := by simp

open QuotientAddGroup

@[simp]
lemma norm_induced {hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁} (f : CoupleSum hC) :
    ‖f‖ = ‖(coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)).quotKerEquivRange.symm f‖ := rfl

lemma norm_eq (hC : InterpolationCouple' 𝕜 F₀ F₁) (f : CoupleSum hC) :
    ‖f‖ = sInf (norm '' { g | coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC) g = f} ) := by
  set T := coupleAdd (Classical.choice hC)
  obtain ⟨g₀, hg₀⟩ : ∃ g, T g = f := f.2
  have h1 : sInf (norm '' {g | T g = f }) = sInf ((fun g ↦ ‖g₀ + g‖) '' {k | T k = 0 }) := by
    congr 1; ext k
    simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨g, hTg, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨g-g₀, by simp only [map_sub, add_sub_cancel, and_true, hTg, <-hg₀, sub_self]⟩
    · rintro ⟨g, hg, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨g+g₀, by simp_rw [ContinuousLinearMap.map_add, hg, <-hg₀,zero_add, add_comm]; simp⟩
  rw [h1, show {k | T k = 0 } = T.ker.toAddSubgroup from rfl, <-quotient_norm_mk_eq _ g₀,
    norm_induced]
  apply congrArg
  apply (LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq (T.quotKerEquivRange)).mpr
  apply Subtype.val_injective
  rw [mk'_apply, SetLike.coe_eq_coe]
  exact SetLike.coe_eq_coe.mp (id (Eq.symm hg₀))
